statement: A cylindrical rain tank has an inside diameter of $6$ feet and an inside height of $10$ feet. One cubic foot holds about $7.48$ gallons. About how many gallons does the tank hold when full?

choices.misconception: I found the volume, about $283$ cubic feet, and then divided by $7.48$ instead of multiplying.
I found the volume in cubic feet, about $283$, and forgot to convert it to gallons.
I used $2\pi r h$, the area of the curved side, instead of the volume $\pi r^2 h$, so I got $60\pi \cdot 7.48 \approx 1{,}410$.

hints: First find the volume of the cylinder in cubic feet.
Use $V = \pi r^2 h$ with the radius, which is half the diameter. Then convert cubic feet to gallons.

solutions.reliable: The radius is $3$ feet, so the volume is $\pi \cdot 3^2 \cdot 10 = 90\pi \approx 282.7$ cubic feet. Each cubic foot holds about $7.48$ gallons, so the tank holds about $282.7 \cdot 7.48 \approx 2{,}115$ gallons.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
